# Discrete Math

![Discrete Math function icon](../../../../assets/function-icons/functions/math/discrete/00_Repertoire%20Discrete%20Math.svg)

[Mathematics functions](../index.md) · [All functions](../../index.md)

GCD, LCM, Factorial, Prime Factor, Check Prime, Permute, Binomial Coefficient and Continued Fraction. Fixed typed signatures; arrays are whole values, not dynamically added terminals. NI reference: classic LabVIEW, not verified NXG. FROG specifies boundary cases and status codes.

## Browse this palette

This entry opens a palette folder; it is not an executable dataflow function.

| Entry | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [GCD](../../math/discrete/gcd.md) | Computes the nonnegative greatest common divisor of two I32 integers. FROG defines gcd(x,0)=abs(x) and gcd(0,0)=0; a magnitude of 2^31 is an I32 overflow, reported without wraparound or a usable result. Formula: gcd(abs(x),abs(y)). Example: GCD(-48,18)=6; GCD(0,0)=0. |
| [LCM](../../math/discrete/lcm.md) | Computes the nonnegative least common multiple of two I32 integers in I64 arithmetic. Returns zero if either input is zero; the widened result can exceed I32 without overflow. Formula: 0 if x==0 or y==0, otherwise abs((x/gcd(x,y))*y). Example: LCM(-12,18)=36; LCM(0,18)=0. |
| [Factorial](../../math/discrete/factorial.md) | Computes n! for an I32 integer, returning F64. FROG defines 0!=1, negative n as NaN with a domain indication and n&gt;=171 as +Infinity with overflow. Large finite factorials may round in F64; this is not the Gamma function. Formula: n! = product(j, j=1..n); 0! = 1. Example: Factorial(5)=120; Factorial(0)=1; Factorial(171)=+Infinity. |
| [Prime Factor](../../math/discrete/prime_factor.md) | Factors the magnitude of an I64 integer into a rank-one I64 array. FROG sorts repeated prime factors in ascending order; +/-1 produce an empty array and zero produces a domain diagnostic without a usable result. Negative inputs use their magnitude, including INT64_MIN. Cancellation or a work limit never returns a partial factorization as success. Formula: product(factors) = abs(n). Example: Prime Factor(-60)=[2,2,3,5]; Prime Factor(1)=[]. |
| [Check Prime](../../math/discrete/check_prime.md) | Returns a Boolean primality result for an I64 integer. Every n&lt;2, including negative values, is False; the magnitude is not substituted. The FROG contract is deterministic on the entire I64 range, not a probabilistic guess. Formula: true iff n is a prime integer &gt;= 2. Example: Check Prime(-7)=False; Check Prime(97)=True; Check Prime(561)=False. |
| [Permute](../../math/discrete/permute.md) | Counts ordered selections of k distinct elements among n, without replacement. Inputs n and k are U32; output nPk is F64. FROG defines k=0 as 1, including (0,0), and k&gt;n as 0. Overflow produces +Infinity; ordinary F64 rounding is allowed. Returns a count, never a reordered array. Formula: P(n,k)=n!/(n-k)! for k&lt;=n; 0 for k&gt;n. Example: Permute(5,2)=20; Permute(1000,2)=999000; Permute(0,0)=1. |
| [Binomial Coefficient](../../math/discrete/binomial.md) | Counts unordered selections of k distinct elements among n. U32 inputs produce an F64 coefficient and a separate I32 status. FROG defines k&gt;n as coefficient=0,error=0; boundaries k=0 or k=n give 1. Finite large coefficients may round. Overflow gives +Infinity,error=2; ordinary success gives error=0. Formula: C(n,k)=n!/(k!*(n-k)!) for k&lt;=n; 0 for k&gt;n. Example: C(5,2)=10; C(5,3)=10; C(5,0)=1. |
| [Continued Fraction](../../math/discrete/continued_fraction.md) | Evaluates the finite rational convergent A[0]/(B[0]+A[1]/(B[1]+...)), using every coefficient. Required A and B are nonempty rank-one F64 arrays of equal length with finite coefficients. Result is F64 with a separate I32 status. Empty/unequal arrays, nonfinite coefficients or a final zero denominator give NaN,error=1; overflow gives an overflow indication. Intermediate zero denominators are not automatically invalid: A=[1,1],B=[2,0] gives 0. This A[0] convention is FROG; NI equation indexing remains unconfirmed. It evaluates supplied coefficients, not a scalar-to-coefficients conversion. Formula: A[0]/(B[0]+A[1]/(B[1]+...+A[m-1]/B[m-1])). Example: A=[3],B=[2] gives 1.5; A=[1,1,1],B=[1,1,1] gives 2/3; A=[2,3,4],B=[5,6,7] gives 92/251. |
